sentences.zh: 如果我们把时间拨到8月26日。所以在8月26日，

sentences.en: 1792, terrible news reaches Paris from the Eastern Front.
sentences.zh: 1792年，巴黎从东线收到了可怕的消息。

sentences.en: The Prussians have been advancing for seven days and they have just taken the fortress at Longhi.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士军队已经推进了七天，他们刚刚攻占了隆维要塞。

sentences.en: After barely a fight, Longhi has surrendered and there's only one fortress left, which is Verdun.
sentences.zh: 几乎没怎么抵抗，隆维就投降了，现在只剩下一座要塞，那就是凡尔登。

sentences.en: So it looks like treason.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来像是叛国。

sentences.en: It looks like treason, exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实很像叛国。

sentences.en: And it looks like the Prussians can't be stopped.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来普鲁士人是不可阻挡的。

sentences.en: Some of the Jundans at this point say, listen, you know, effectively it's 1940.
sentences.zh: 此时，一些吉伦特派的人说，听着，你知道的，这实际上就是1940年。

sentences.en: We need to evacuate the government to Tor.
sentences.zh: 我们需要把政府撤退到图尔。

sentences.en: Which is a terrible, I mean, a fateful decision for them to push because Tor is a very royalist and a bubble Catholic city, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这对于他们来说，我的意思是，是一个决定命运的糟糕决定，因为图尔是一个非常保皇、充满天主教气息的城市，不是吗？

sentences.en: So not a sensible place for them to choose if they're in a life or death struggle with people on the, on further to the left.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们正与左翼人士进行生死搏斗，这绝不是一个明智的选择。

sentences.en: Yeah, it looks weak.
sentences.zh: 是的，这显得很软弱。

sentences.en: Well, it looks royaliSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这显得很保皇。

sentences.en: It looks like they're not invested actually in the defence of Paris.
sentences.zh: 这看起来他们实际上并不关心巴黎的防卫。

sentences.en: Rob Spear says, no way we should stand and fight in the defence of liberty.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔说，绝不可能，我们应该坚守并为捍卫自由而战。

sentences.en: And of course, the Minister of Justice, this sort of big, fleshy, sort of corrupt, but very charismatic revolutionary leader.
sentences.zh: 当然还有司法大臣，这个身材魁梧、略显腐败，但非常有个人魅力的革命领袖。

sentences.en: Another man with skin probleMs. And people who've listened to our first two seasons may remember that skin problems feature throughout this.
sentences.zh: 又一个有皮肤问题的人。听过我们前两季的听众可能还记得，皮肤问题贯穿了整个节目。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say, he's got terrible skin and he's got a taste for a brown envelope.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以客观地说，他的皮肤糟透了，而且他还喜欢收黑钱。

sentences.en: You know, he likes, he likes a backhander that he can spend on a mistress and a massive selection of starters.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他喜欢，他喜欢能用来包养情妇和买一大堆开胃菜的贿赂。

sentences.en: That's Danton's modus operandi.
sentences.zh: 这就是丹东的行事风格。

sentences.en: Danton basically seizes the moment and he says, close the city gates of Paris, put up barricades.
sentences.zh: 丹东基本上抓住了时机，他说，关闭巴黎城门，竖起路障。

sentences.en: I want, I want volunteers.
sentences.zh: 我要，我要志愿者。

sentences.en: I'm on recruiting stations everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处建立招募站。

sentences.en: And his charisma, his Churchillian charisma is really important, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为他的个人魅力，他那丘吉尔式的魅力真的很重要。

sentences.en: Sort of steadying the nerves.
sentences.zh: 这起到了稳定军心的作用。

sentences.en: I mean, he really rises to meet the moment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他真的是临危受命。

sentences.en: But there is a dark side to all these preparations because the provisional government, with Danton as its kind of leading light, issues an official proclamation at this point.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些准备工作都有黑暗的一面，因为以丹东为核心的临时政府，在此时发布了一份官方公告。

sentences.en: And it says, yeah, watch out for the Prussians, but also watch out for the enemies within.
sentences.zh: 公告说，是的，要防范普鲁士人，但也要防范内部的敌人。

sentences.en: Citizens, you have traitors in your bosom, but for them, the fight would already be over.
sentences.zh: 公民们，你们的怀里藏着叛徒，要不是他们，战斗早就结束了。

sentences.en: Your active surveillance cannot fail to defeat them.
sentences.zh: 你们的积极监视一定能打败他们。

sentences.en: Now, what do they mean by the traitors within?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们所说的内部叛徒是什么意思？

sentences.en: They mean corrupt former advisors to the king, ladies in waiting at the court who they say are all lesbians, speculators, hoarders, criminals,
sentences.zh: 他们指的是国王腐败的前顾问、宫廷里被他们说成全是女同性恋的宫廷女官、投机商、囤积居奇者、罪犯，

sentences.en: the old Swiss guards, priests who have defied the civil constitution of the clergy, journalists who have written in defence of the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 老瑞士卫队、违抗神职人员民事宪法的神甫、为君主制辩护的记者。

sentences.en: All these people, they think, are in the pay effectively of the sinister Austrian committee that is masterminded by Marie Antoinette and her friends in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人，他们认为，实际上都是由玛丽·安托瓦内特和她在维也纳的朋友们所策划的阴险的奥地利委员会的收买对象。

sentences.en: I mean, that's pretty much the case, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上就是这样，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: And on the issue of Marie Antoinette and her friends in Vienna, I mean, they're not wrong because Marie Antoinette has been conniving with the
sentences.zh: 至于玛丽·安托瓦内特和她在维也纳的朋友们这个问题，我的意思是，他们没有猜错，因为玛丽·安托瓦内特一直在与

sentences.en: Austrians.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人勾结。

sentences.en: So that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, it's important to say that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: So by the 28th of August, two days later, Danton has now ordered raids across the city, raids on people's houses.
sentences.zh: 所以到了8月28日，也就是两天后，丹东下令在全城进行搜查，搜查人们的住所。

sentences.en: They're searching for guns.
sentences.zh: 他们在搜寻枪支。

sentences.en: They're searching for enemy agents, stolen documents, letters.
sentences.zh: 他们在搜寻敌方特工、被盗文件、信件。

sentences.en: So if you've ever seen documentaries or films about the French Revolution, you've seen this sort of quite
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你看过关于法国大革命的纪录片或电影，你就会看到这种非常

sentences.en: stereotypical image of a group of sans-culottes with their kind of red hats and their pikes banging on people's doors.
sentences.zh: 刻板的形象：一群穿着长裤、戴着红帽子、拿着长矛的无套裤汉在砸人们的门。

sentences.en: Thick stubble.
sentences.zh: 长满浓密的胡茬。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You've got an Aristo hidden in the cellar or something.
sentences.zh: 地下室里藏着一个贵族什么的。

sentences.en: That's where this is coming from.
sentences.zh: 这就是出处所在。

sentences.en: Lots of historians at this point cite a diarist called
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，许多历史学家引用了一位名叫

sentences.en: Rosalie Julien.
sentences.zh: 罗莎莉·朱利安的日记作者。

sentences.en: She's a brilliant diarist, actually, on this period because she is married to a Jacobin deputy.
sentences.zh: 实际上，她是这一时期非常出色的日记作家，因为她嫁给了一位雅各宾派议员。

sentences.en: Now, she is somebody who really complicates your sense of the French
sentences.zh: 现在，她是一个真正让你的法国

sentences.en: Revolution.
sentences.zh: 大革命观感变得复杂的人。

sentences.en: She's a very likable character.
sentences.zh: 她是一个非常讨人喜欢的人物。

sentences.en: She's very well read.
sentences.zh: 她博览群书。

sentences.en: She's very educated.
sentences.zh: 她受过良好的教育。

sentences.en: She's a big fan of Rousseau, a massive do-gooder and a reformer.
sentences.zh: 她是卢梭的超级粉丝，是一个极大的慈善家和改革者。

sentences.en: But she is always writing in her diary, the city is full of traitors and we have to root them out.
sentences.zh: 但她总是在日记里写道，这座城市充满了叛徒，我们必须把他们根除。

sentences.en: Still more traitors, still more treason.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的叛徒，更多的叛国行为。

sentences.en: And I think those words are really important to understand what's going to happen because she and so many other people are saying they're all in the prisons.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些话对于理解接下来要发生的事情非常重要，因为她和许多其他人都在说他们全都在监狱里。

sentences.en: All of these prisons are stuffed with traitors.
sentences.zh: 所有这些监狱里都塞满了叛徒。

sentences.en: And as soon as our troops, you know, these volunteers march out to face the Prussians, the traitors will seize their moment.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们的部队，你知道的，这些志愿者开赴前线对抗普鲁士人，叛徒们就会抓住时机。

sentences.en: They will break out and massacre the women and children of Paris.
sentences.zh: 他们会冲出来，屠杀巴黎的妇女和儿童。

sentences.en: About half a year ago, we did the Battle of Agincourt and Henry V is facing the French army, but he's taken lots of prisoners.
sentences.zh: 大约半年前，我们讲过阿金库尔战役，亨利五世面对的是法国军队，但他俘虏了许多囚犯。

sentences.en: And when he thinks that he's being attacked from the rear, he orders the prisoners killed because obviously the enemy within is highly dangerous.
sentences.zh: 当他认为自己遭到后方袭击时，他下令杀死囚犯，因为很显然，内奸是极其危险的。

sentences.en: And there's a slight, I mean, comparing the French Revolution to the Battle of Agincourt, not probably something
sentences.zh: 而且有一种轻微的，我的意思是，把法国大革命与阿金库尔战役进行比较，可能

sentences.en: anyone's ever done before, but there's a slight element of that to it, I think.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人这样做过，但我想其中确实有那么一点点相似之处。

sentences.en: I think it totally is, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我完全这么认为。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think there's a sense of the stab in the back is coming.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有一种背后捅刀子的感觉即将来临。

sentences.en: And there were all these rumours about breakouts in the prisons.
sentences.zh: 而且当时有各种关于监狱越狱的传言。

sentences.en: So all through August, actually, there had been rumours, the Paris police had been reporting rumours that people were about to break
sentences.zh: 事实上，整个八月期间一直有传言，巴黎警方一直在报告传言，称有人正准备闯入

sentences.en: into the prisons and I quote, render prompt justice to the people inside them.
sentences.zh: 监狱，用我的话说，对里面的人实施迅速的审判。

sentences.en: And in fact, it's not surprising that the Paris police are reporting that because some newspapers and radical
sentences.zh: 事实上，巴黎警方会报告这一点并不令人意外，因为一些报纸、激进的

sentences.en: pamphlets and posters and things are very, very explicit about what they think we should do.
sentences.zh: 小册子和海报等对他们认为我们应该做什么表达得非常非常明确。

sentences.en: And I'll just give you two examples.
sentences.zh: 我只举两个例子。

sentences.en: So one is a newspaper called the Orator of the People, and it was edited by a guy called Fréron, who's a friend of Camille Desmoulins, who we've talked about before.
sentences.zh: 其中一份报纸叫《人民演说家》，由一个叫弗雷隆的人编辑，他是卡米尔·德穆兰的朋友，我们以前谈起过他。

sentences.en: Fréron wrote this, the first battle we shall fight will be inside the walls of Paris, not outside.
sentences.zh: 弗雷隆写道，我们要打的第一场仗是在巴黎城内，而不是城外。

sentences.en: All the royal brigands clustering inside this unhappy town will perish in the same day.
sentences.zh: 聚集在这个不幸城镇内的所有保皇党强盗将在同一天灭亡。

sentences.en: The prisons are full of conspirators.
sentences.zh: 监狱里挤满了阴谋家。

sentences.en: Let the world see how we judge them.
sentences.zh: 让世界看看我们是如何审判他们的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's ominous, but not as ominous as this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很不祥，但还没有这个不祥。

sentences.en: This is from a guy called Fabre Desglantine, who was a friend, a great friend of Danton and who was a poet.
sentences.zh: 这段话来自一个叫法布尔·代格朗蒂纳的人，他是丹东的朋友，一位好朋友，也是一位诗人。

sentences.en: He's not a great ornament, I think, to the poetic profession when you read his words.
sentences.zh: 当你读他的文字时，我认为他在诗歌界算不上什么大人物。

sentences.en: Let us clear the ranks of these vile slaves of tyranny.
sentences.zh: 让我们清除暴政这些卑鄙奴隶的行列。

sentences.en: Let the blood of traitors be the first holocaust to liberty.
sentences.zh: 让叛徒的鲜血成为献给自由的第一场大屠杀。

sentences.en: I mean, he literally used the phrase le premier holocaust, so that in advancing to meet the common enemy, we leave nothing behind to disquiet us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他字面意思使用了“le premier holocaust”这个词，这样我们在向前迎击共同的敌人时，就不会留下任何让我们不安的后患。

sentences.en: And actually,
sentences.zh: 事实上，

sentences.en: Marat, one of the most outspoken of all these journalists.
sentences.zh: 马拉，所有这些记者中最直言不讳的一个。

sentences.en: And has the worst skin.
sentences.zh: 而且皮肤最差。

sentences.en: Not coincidentally, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝非巧合。

sentences.en: Marat says, basically, citizens should go to the Abbey prison, get the prisoners, and I quote, run them through with a sword.
sentences.zh: 马拉基本上说，公民们应该去阿拜伊监狱，把囚犯抓出来，用我的话说，用剑捅死他们。

sentences.en: And some of Marat's kind of defenders in the historical profession say, oh, that's just Marat.
sentences.zh: 历史学界中马拉的一些捍卫者说，哦，那只是马拉。

sentences.en: You know, he talks, he doesn't really mean it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他只是说说，他并不是真的想这么做。

sentences.en: But as Simon Sharma says, you know, how do you know?
sentences.zh: 但正如西蒙·沙玛所说，你知道的，你怎么知道？

sentences.en: How are people supposed to tell the difference?
sentences.zh: 人们怎么去分辨区别？

sentences.en: So this is the climate.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时的氛围。

sentences.en: On the 29th of August, the Prussians reach Verdun.
sentences.zh: 8月29日，普鲁士军队抵达凡尔登。

sentences.en: And Verdun is the keystone of France's eastern defensive line.
sentences.zh: 凡尔登是法国东部防御线的基石。

sentences.en: If you get past Verdun, you're into the valley of the Marne.
sentences.zh: 如果你过了凡尔登，你就进入了马恩河谷。

sentences.en: And once you go through that, you are heading towards Paris.
sentences.zh: 一旦穿过那里，你就在朝着巴黎前进。

sentences.en: And Verdun surrenders after three days to this impregnable fortress.
sentences.zh: 三天后，这座坚不可摧的要塞凡尔登投降了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The garrison commander who'd said he'd never surrender either kills himself or is killed by the people of Verdun, who basically don't fancy a siege at all.
sentences.zh: 那位曾说绝不投降的守备司令要么自杀了，要么被凡尔登的人民杀死了，这些人根本不想经历围城战。

sentences.en: We're like, yeah, we'll let the Prussians in.
sentences.zh: 我们当时就像是，好吧，我们放普鲁士人进来吧。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 行吧。

sentences.en: So Verdun surrenders and the news arrives in Paris on Sunday, the 2nd of
sentences.zh: 所以凡尔登投降了，消息于9月2日星期日传到了

sentences.en: September.
sentences.zh: 巴黎。

sentences.en: The Prussians are broken through.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士人突破了防线。

sentences.en: And now you've got, I mean, it's an extraordinary scene.
sentences.zh: 现在你看到了，我的意思是，这是一场非同寻常的场景。

sentences.en: You have kind of church bells ringing.
sentences.zh: 你会听到教堂的钟声在敲响。

sentences.en: There are cannons on the Revassane sounding the alert.
sentences.zh: 雷瓦萨纳的大炮正在鸣炮警报。

sentences.en: And this is when Danton gives his Churchillian address.
sentences.zh: 这就是丹东发表他那篇丘吉尔式演讲的时候。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Danton gives his address.
sentences.zh: 丹东发表了他的演讲。

sentences.en: There are posters going up across the city to arms, arms to arMs. The enemy is at the gates.
sentences.zh: 全城贴满了海报：拿起武器，拿起武器。敌人就在城门外。

sentences.en: Now, that afternoon, we can be pretty sure that something else happened, but we can't be exactly certain what, because the documents were later destroyed.
sentences.zh: 那天下午，我们可以确信还发生了别的事，但无法确切知道是什么，因为文件后来被销毁了。

sentences.en: They were destroyed in the events of 1870-71.
sentences.zh: 它们在1870-1871年的事件中被毁了。

sentences.en: It's ironic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很讽刺，不是吗？

sentences.en: Another Prussian day trip to Paris.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士人又一次巴黎一日游。

sentences.en: So what seems to have happened is that some of the sections, these are the kind of neighbourhood councils in Paris, discussed how we eliminate these people in the prisons.
sentences.zh: 所以似乎发生的事情是，一些区委员会（也就是巴黎的街区理事会）讨论了如何消灭监狱里的这些人。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of people saying it's an unpleasant necessity, but basically somebody has to do it.
sentences.zh: 有很多人说这是一个令人不快但必要的选择，但基本上总得有人来做这件事。

sentences.en: Now, that's not to say the sections ordered it, but the tone has kind of been set.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说各区下达了命令，但基调已经定下了。

sentences.en: About this point, the chief prison inspector comes to Danton on the Hotel de Ville and City Hall, and he says, I'm genuinely worried about the safety of the people in the prisons.
sentences.zh: 大约在这个时候，首席监狱巡视员来到市政厅找到丹东，他说，我真心担心监狱里人们的安全。

sentences.en: And Danton says, je me fous bien des prisonniers.
sentences.zh: 丹东说：“je me fous bien des prisonniers。”

sentences.en: I don't give a damn about the prisoners.
sentences.zh: 我才不在乎囚犯的死活。

sentences.en: Like, basically let them fend for themselves.
sentences.zh: 就像是，基本上让他们自生自灭吧。

sentences.en: But to be fair to him, I mean, one of the reasons for that is that he can't spare people from the barricades.
sentences.zh: 但平心而论，我的意思是，原因之一是他不能从路障那里抽调人手。

sentences.en: There's only a finite number of people, and obviously the main threat from his perspective is the approach of the Prussian.
sentences.zh: 人数是有限的，显然从他的角度来看，最大的威胁是普鲁士军队的逼近。

sentences.en: Tom, I'm so surprised at this.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我对这一点感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: I thought you were going to be on the other side of this equation, but it's very clear to me now, from the way you've conducted yourself in this whole
sentences.zh: 我本以为你会站在问题的另一边，但现在从你在这整集节目中的表现来看，很显然，你知道的，你将采取一种非常类似多米尼克·桑德布鲁克在塔中王子问题上的立场，对吧？

sentences.en: episode, that, you know, you're going to take a very Dominic Sandbrook, the princes in the tower, lying on this issue, are you?
sentences.zh: （译注：此处“the princes in the tower, lying on this issue”对应播客中常见的历史争议隐喻）

sentences.en: Well, no, but I do think that there are reasons why someone like Danton, people in charge of the revolution, might be unconcerned with prisoners and the security of the prisoners
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，但我确实认为，像丹东这样的人、革命的负责人之所以可能不关心囚犯和囚犯的安全，是有原因的，

sentences.en: that relates to the overall situation in Paris.
sentences.zh: 这与巴黎的整体局势有关。

sentences.en: Yeah, fair enough.
sentences.zh: 好吧，有道理。

sentences.en: And also, don't forget, everybody thinks the prisoners are total villains and traitors and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且别忘了，每个人都认为囚犯是大恶人、叛徒以及诸如此类的人。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But I think that saying, you know, we can't bother with them, it's justified by military exigencies.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，说什么我们无暇顾及他们，是由军事紧迫性所决定的。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: Listeners can make up their own minds, can't they?
sentences.zh: 听众可以自己做判断，不是吗？

sentences.en: I have to say, Theo agrees with you.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，西奥同意你的看法。

sentences.en: He's written in the chat, well said, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他在聊天里写道，说得好，汤姆。

sentences.en: So that's nice.
sentences.zh: 所以这挺好的。

sentences.en: So let's get into the story.
sentences.zh: 那么我们进入正题。

sentences.en: Sometime about 2.30 that afternoon, the 2nd of September, the news has come in from Verdun.
sentences.zh: 9月2那天下午大约两点半，凡尔登的消息传来了。

sentences.en: There was a group of prisoners being escorted through the city from the
sentences.zh: 有一群囚犯正被押送穿过城市，从

sentences.en: Palais de Justice to the Abbe prison.
sentences.zh: 司法宫前往阿拜伊监狱。

sentences.en: And they are royal officials, they're courtiers and they're Catholic priests.
sentences.zh: 他们是皇室官员、朝臣和天主教神甫。

sentences.en: The streets are obviously packed with people because of the war panic.
sentences.zh: 由于战争恐慌，街上显然挤满了人。

sentences.en: And a lot of people shout abuse at them as they pass in these kind of carriages.
sentences.zh: 当他们坐着这种马车经过时，许多人对他们恶语相向。

sentences.en: As they get towards the Abbe prison, which is in Saint-Germain-des-Prés, it's a former
sentences.zh: 当他们到达位于圣日耳曼德普雷的拉贝监狱时，这是一个前

sentences.en: Abbe, hence the name, a group of people stop them.
sentences.zh: 拉贝修道院，名字也由此而来，一群人拦住了他们。

sentences.en: These people are National Guardsmen, sans-culottes, a mixture of characters.
sentences.zh: 这些人是国民自卫军、无套裤汉，成分十分杂乱。

sentences.en: They stop the carriages, they drag the prisoners out and they drag them into the nearby section headquarters, which is a convent.
sentences.zh: 他们拦下马车，把囚犯拖出来，拖到附近的一个区指挥部，那是一座修道院。

sentences.en: And there's a great crowd of people there and the people are shouting, these are enemies of the people, you know, why take them to the prison?
sentences.zh: 那里聚集了大量人群，人们在高喊，这些是人民的敌人，你知道的，为什么要把他们带到监狱里？

sentences.en: Why not just get rid of them now?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在不直接除掉他们？

sentences.en: Two or three of those prisoners try to break out, try to get away or fight for their lives or whatever.
sentences.zh: 其中两三个囚犯试图突围、逃跑、为生命而战或做点别的。

sentences.en: There's a scuffle, they're beaten up and they are hacked to death with knives and their bodies are left in the courtyard.
sentences.zh: 现场发生了一场混战，他们遭到殴打，被刀砍死，尸体被丢在庭院里。

sentences.en: The rest of the prisoners are just, you know,
sentences.zh: 其余的囚犯只是，你知道的，

sentences.en: 20 people or so are just standing there absolutely traumatized in shock, wondering what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 大约20个人站在那里，完全陷入了创伤和震惊之中，不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: An impromptu tribunal is set up and it declares them guilty.
sentences.zh: 一个临时法庭建立起来了，宣判他们有罪。

sentences.en: Then one by one, in a very methodical way, they're led down the steps into the garden and there a group of men has assembled with knives, axes, hatchets.
sentences.zh: 然后，他们一个接一个、非常按部就班地被带下台阶进入花园，那里聚集了一群拿着刀、斧子和短斧的人。

sentences.en: There's a guy who's like clearly a carpenter because he's brought his saw and one by one they are hacked to death.
sentences.zh: 有一个人显然是个木匠，因为他带来了锯子，他们一个接一个地被砍死。

sentences.en: It's important to say right from the beginning, this is the first incident.
sentences.zh: 一开始必须说明的是，这是第一起事件。

sentences.en: It is not a mad frenzy.
sentences.zh: 这并不是疯狂的狂热。

sentences.en: It's not an orgy of violence.
sentences.zh: 这不是一场暴力的狂欢。

sentences.en: It is quiet.
sentences.zh: 它是安静的。

sentences.en: It's considered.
sentences.zh: 它是经过深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: The guys take their time.
sentences.zh: 这些家伙不慌不忙。

sentences.en: It takes about half an hour to kill all these men and then it is done.
sentences.zh: 杀死所有这些男人大约花了半个小时，然后就结束了。

sentences.en: And upstairs, the people who are still there, the room is absolutely full of people and they are debating, now that we've killed these people, why don't we just go
sentences.zh: 而在楼上，那些还在那里的人，房间里绝对挤满了人，他们在争论，既然我们已经杀这些人，为什么不直接走进

sentences.en: into the Abbey prison and do the same with everybody who is in there?
sentences.zh: 阿贝监狱，对里面所有人也如法炮制呢？

sentences.en: But again, not necessarily to kill them, to sit in judgment on them.
sentences.zh: 但同样，不一定是杀死他们，而是对他们进行审判。

sentences.en: As we'll see, not everybody is killed.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，并不是所有人都被杀死了。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: While that crowd is all debating and arguing about how they're going to do it, a separate group breaks into another prison about a mile away called the the Karm.
sentences.zh: 正当那群人在争论和辩论他们将如何行动时，另一拨人闯入了大约一英里外的一座名为加姆的监狱。

sentences.en: It's a former Karmelite convent.
sentences.zh: 这是一座前加尔默罗修道院。

sentences.en: So a lot of these prisons are convents and abbeys and religious houses that have been converted.
sentences.zh: 所以很多这样的监狱都是由修道院、修院和宗教机构改造而成的。

sentences.en: In this prison, there are about 160 priests.
sentences.zh: 在这座监狱里，大约有160名神父。

sentences.en: This crowd again organizes a kind of improvised tribunal.
sentences.zh: 这群人再次组织了一个类似即兴的法庭。

sentences.en: They call out the prisoners' names one by one.
sentences.zh: 他们一个接一个地喊出囚犯的名字。

sentences.en: They take them out into the garden.
sentences.zh: 他们把他们带到花园里。

sentences.en: Some of them are shot.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人被枪决了。

sentences.en: Most of them, though, are hacked to death again.
sentences.zh: 不过，大多数人还是被砍死了。

sentences.en: Some of them try to climb over the walls or they even climb trees to get away.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人试图翻墙，甚至爬上树逃跑。

sentences.en: But they are dragged back and finished off with knives.
sentences.zh: 但他们被拖了回来，用刀结果了生命。

sentences.en: Again, just to say, I mean, a quarter of them are spared.
sentences.zh: 再强调一次，我是说，四分之一的人被放过了。

sentences.en: Well, hold on.
sentences.zh: 等等，稍等。

sentences.en: 115 people out of 160 are killed in this.
sentences.zh: 160人中有115人在这次事件中被杀。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Because I think it's easy to think that it is a total massacre.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为人们很容易认为这是一场彻底的大屠杀。

sentences.en: Well, you wouldn't take your chances with that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你不会去冒这个险的。

sentences.en: Of course not.
sentences.zh: 当然不会。

sentences.en: It's just really supporting what you were saying, that this isn't a kind of frothing at the mouth, mad mob frenzy.
sentences.zh: 这只是在印证你刚才的说法，即这并非那种气急败坏、疯狂的暴民狂热。

sentences.en: It's much more considered.
sentences.zh: 这是经过更多深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: And therefore, I think actually much more frightening than that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为这实际上比那更加可怕。

sentences.en: Agreed.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: And by the way, we both gave different figures.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们俩给出了不同的数字。

sentences.en: That's not because one of us is right and the other is wrong.
sentences.zh: 那并不是因为我们中有一个人对而另一个错。

sentences.en: It's because every history book gives different figures on this.
sentences.zh: 这是因为每一本历史书对此给出的数字都不同。

sentences.en: So yeah, there is a lot of confusion about the figures.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，关于这些数字有很多混乱的说法。

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, the death squad has got started in the Abbe prison and also in some of the other prisons.
sentences.zh: 同时，行刑队已经在阿贝监狱以及其他一些监狱开始了行动。

sentences.en: And in all of them, it is the same kind of routine.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些监狱里，都是同样的套路。

sentences.en: I think actually death squad is better than mob.
sentences.zh: 我觉得“行刑队”这个词实际上比“暴民”更好。

sentences.en: They're often described as mobs, but these are kind of organized teams of men.
sentences.zh: 他们经常被描述为暴民，但这些是有组织的小组。

sentences.en: They almost always hold this kind of tribunal.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎总是举行这种法庭审判。

sentences.en: They bring people out into the courtyard once they've been found guilty, and then they stab them or hack them to death.
sentences.zh: 一旦被判有罪，他们就会把人带到庭院里，然后用刀刺死或砍死他们。

sentences.en: And we only know one of the names of the people who organized this, a guy called
sentences.zh: 我们只知道组织这件事的其中一个人的名字，一个叫

sentences.en: Stanislas Maillard, who was a clerk.
sentences.zh: 斯坦尼斯拉斯·迈拉尔的人，他曾是一名书记员。

sentences.en: He'd been at the Bastille.
sentences.zh: 他曾去过巴士底狱。

sentences.en: He'd been a big figure in the
sentences.zh: 他曾是其中一个重要人物

sentences.en: Women's March on Versailles.
sentences.zh: 凡尔赛妇女进军。

sentences.en: And he seems to have been one of those people who's thrown up by these periods of revolution and kind of chaos.
sentences.zh: 他似乎正是那种在革命和混乱时期被这些时期抛上风口浪尖的人。

sentences.en: So a bit of a bully.
sentences.zh: 所以有点像个恶霸。

sentences.en: You know, you could say he's the kind of person who would be a paramilitary leader.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，可以说他就是那种会成为准军事武装领袖的人。

sentences.en: And he loves all this.
sentences.zh: 他很喜欢这一切。

sentences.en: And he's obviously, this is his moment.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这就是他的高光时刻。

sentences.en: But it's interesting, isn't it, that actually so few names are known.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，居然有这么少的名字被流传下来。

sentences.en: And in large part, that is because in due course, to be at Septembriseur, as they come to be called, is highly dangerous,
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是因为，后来被称为“九月屠杀参与者”（Septembriseur）是一件非常危险的事，

sentences.en: because it comes to be seen as a terrible blot on the reputation of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 因为这后来被视为革命声誉上的一个可怕污点。

sentences.en: Not immediately, though.
sentences.zh: 不过不是马上就觉得是。

sentences.en: And I think that that reflects the fact that this is genuinely not being organized by the big names, by Danton, Robespierre, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了一个事实，即这确实不是由大人物——比如丹东、罗伯斯庇尔等人——组织起来的。

sentences.en: It's coming probably from the sections.
sentences.zh: 它可能来自各个区。

sentences.en: And the people who are organizing it are not people who will go on to great things to become kind of famous names.
sentences.zh: 组织它的人并不是那些后来成就大业、成为大名鼎鼎人物的人。

sentences.en: I think you're absolutely right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得你完全说对了。

sentences.en: I think he is being organized.
sentences.zh: 我认为它确实是有人在组织的。

sentences.en: And insofar as there is a sense of organization, it's at a very, very sort of low level.
sentences.zh: 就存在某种组织感而言，它处在非常非常低的层面上。

sentences.en: It's these kind of neighborhood councils.
sentences.zh: 就是这种社区委员会。

sentences.en: The commune, we know that they talked about, that's an instructionary council that's taking control of Paris.
sentences.zh: 公社，我们知道他们讨论过，那是一个接管巴黎的起义委员会。

sentences.en: We know they talked about it and they said, your point, there weren't enough men to protect the prisons.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们讨论过，他们说，正如你所提到的，没有足够的人手来保护监狱。

sentences.en: We need them on the barricades.
sentences.zh: 我们需要他们在街垒上。

sentences.en: One of the commune's committees issued a statement signed by Marat, the prisoners are brigands who will slaughter our children and our women.
sentences.zh: 公社的一个委员会发表了一份声明，由马拉签署，囚犯们是会屠杀我们的孩子和妇女的强盗。

sentences.en: These acts of justice are indispensable to deter through the use of terror these legions of traitors.
sentences.zh: 这些正义行动是不可或缺的，旨在通过恐怖手段震慑这些叛徒军团。

sentences.en: But it's not like Marat is being named as a guy who's leading it.
sentences.zh: 但马拉并没有被点名是领导者。

sentences.en: No, no, he's not going in.
sentences.zh: 不，不，他没有亲自进去。

sentences.en: He's inspired it.
sentences.zh: 他是启发了这一切。

sentences.en: But I think these are basically the people who had attacked the Tuileries, right?
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这些人基本上就是袭击杜伊勒利宫的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，我想是的。

sentences.en: It's people from the working class areas of Paris.
sentences.zh: 他们来自巴黎的工人阶级区。

sentences.en: They are representative figures from the working population of Paris.
sentences.zh: 他们是巴黎劳动人口的代表性人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，我也这么认为。

sentences.en: I mean, and we'll talk about in the second half about what the population of Paris think of it, but I think you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在下半场会讨论巴黎民众对此的看法，但我认为你绝对说对了。

sentences.en: They're basically are pretty representative of the city and of the streets, I guess.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上可以说是这座城市和街头的典型代表。

sentences.en: It is the vengeance of the streets.
sentences.zh: 这是街头的复仇。

sentences.en: That's what historians who are more sympathetic to the September massacre say.
sentences.zh: 那些对九月大屠杀抱有更多同情心的历史学家就是这么说的。

sentences.en: I mean, on the bigwigs, the bigwigs know this is happening, but they don't do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，大人物们，大人物们知道这件事正在发生，但他们什么也没做。

sentences.en: Danton says to Brissot, Durandant leader, the deaths are an indispensable sacrifice to appease the people of Paris.
sentences.zh: 丹东对吉伦特派领袖布里索说，这些死刑是安抚巴黎人民不可或缺的牺牲。

sentences.en: The interior minister, Jean-Marie Roulon, the husband of Madame Roulon, the great sort of lynchpin of the Girondin sort of social circle.
sentences.zh: 内政部长让-马里·罗兰，罗兰夫人的丈夫，吉伦特派社交圈的重要核心人物。

sentences.en: He says the people terrible in its vengeance is exercising a kind of justice.
sentences.zh: 他说，人民在复仇时是可怕的，正在行使一种正义。

sentences.en: You know, they're making excuses for it and kind of, I mean, they do nothing about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们在为之辩解，而且，我是说，他们什么也没做。

sentences.en: That association of terror with a kind of justice, I think is exactly what's happening.
sentences.zh: 我认为，恐怖与某种正义的这种结合，正是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that was very French Revolution, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得这非常具有法国大革命的色彩，不是吗？

sentences.en: So that's the first day.
sentences.zh: 所以那是第一天。

sentences.en: But of course, it's just the first several days.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这只是最初的几天。

sentences.en: The next day, you get to Monday the 3rd.
sentences.zh: 第二天，就到了9月3日星期一。

sentences.en: The men at the
sentences.zh: 在

sentences.en: Abbe Prison, the first prison to be targeted.
sentences.zh: 阿贝监狱——首个被盯上的监狱——的人们。

sentences.en: They're there for about 24 hours working away.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里工作了大约24个小时。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, other men have moved on to other prisons.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，其他人已经转移到了其他监狱。

sentences.en: There's a seminary called Saint-Famain, which holds priests.
sentences.zh: 有一座关押神父的修道院叫圣菲曼。

sentences.en: There's a convent called Saint-Bernard.
sentences.zh: 有一座修道院叫圣伯纳德。

sentences.en: There's an asylum at Bicetre, which holds petty criminals.
sentences.zh: 比塞特尔有一处收容惯犯的精神病院。

sentences.en: Perhaps most shockingly, the Saupetrière Women's Hospice, which holds prostitutes.
sentences.zh: 也许最令人震惊的是收容妓女的萨佩特里埃妇女收容所。

sentences.en: And people have been joking, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 人们一直在开玩笑，不是吗？

sentences.en: We should send Marie Antoinette to the Saupetrière.
sentences.zh: 我们应该把玛丽·安托瓦内特送进萨佩特里埃。

sentences.en: So there, we're not talking about priests or courtiers or, you know, royalist journalists.
sentences.zh: 所以在这里，我们谈论的不是神父、朝臣，或者你知道的保王党记者。

sentences.en: These people are actually poor, petty criminals, prostitutes and so on.
sentences.zh: 这些人实际上是穷人、小罪犯、妓女等等。

sentences.en: And this is, I think, where it gets particularly shocking.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这正是事情变得格外令人震惊的地方。

sentences.en: So be set.
sentences.zh: 所以比塞特尔。

sentences.en: They killed probably 150,
sentences.zh: 他们大概杀死了150、

sentences.en: 160 people.
A lot of them are very young.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人非常年轻。

sentences.en: About 40 of them are probably under 18.
sentences.zh: 他们中大约40人不到18岁。

sentences.en: One of them is 12, two of them are 13, three of them are 14 and so on.
sentences.zh: 其中一个12岁，两个13岁，三个14岁，以此类推。

sentences.en: Saint-Bernard, the people who are killed there, perhaps 70 of them, they're forgers.
sentences.zh: 圣伯纳德，在那里被杀的人，大约70人，他们是伪造犯。

sentences.en: And the Saint-Colot hate forgers because of the paper money.
sentences.zh: 无套裤汉痛恨伪造犯，因为纸币的缘故。

sentences.en: They think the paper money is all a plot.
sentences.zh: 他们认为纸币全是一个阴谋。

sentences.en: They think that the forgers have been working with counter-revolutionaries to undermine it and to drive up grain prices.
sentences.zh: 他们认为伪造犯一直与反革命分子勾结，以破坏纸币并推高粮食价格。

sentences.en: So if you're a forger, you've got to go.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是个伪造犯，你就死定了。

sentences.en: So David Andress, who's written a wonderful book on the terror, he comments on this laconically,
sentences.zh: 因此，写过一本关于恐怖统治的精彩书籍的大卫·安德里斯对此简洁地评论道：

sentences.en: September 1792 was not a good time to be a captured forger.

sentences.zh: 汤姆，其实我认为，也许自1789年以来——我对革命前的巴黎了解不多——

sentences.en: And that's a huge fear of brigands, isn't it?

sentences.en: Well, I think in Paris, there has been the same thing with criminals, you know, an anxiety about street crime and a
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为在巴黎，对罪犯也是一样的情况，你知道的，对街头犯罪的焦虑以及

sentences.en: belief that crime in some obscure way is connected with the court.

sentences.en: Well, again, David Andress, he makes the comment in his book on the terror that there were always 30,000 of them for some reason.

sentences.en: And clearly, it's just part of the temper of the time.

sentences.zh: 人们觉得她非常高傲，对吧？

sentences.en: I think that's because she's shy.
sentences.zh: 我想那是因为她害羞。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She's a nervous person, sickly.
sentences.zh: 她性格神经质，体弱多病。

sentences.en: Socially maladroit.
sentences.zh: 社交笨拙。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: But as you've said and as you brilliantly described in those episodes about Marie Antoinette at the very beginning of the whole French Revolution,
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，也正如你在整个法国大革命初期关于玛丽·安托瓦内特的那些单集里所精彩描述的那样，

sentences.en: cycle, she has always played a very prominent part in the kind of pornographic demonology of the court.
sentences.zh: 她在宫廷那种色情化的妖魔化风气中一直扮演着非常突出的角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And I think this is so important for understanding the things that will come to be written about her death is that Paris has been saturated in appalling pornographic fantasies about Marie Antoinette and about her female attendants and friends.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于理解后来关于她之死的种种记载至关重要，因为巴黎当时充斥着关于玛丽·安托瓦内特以及她的女侍从和朋友们的骇人色情幻想。

sentences.en: And this provides a kind of terrible context for what will happen to her and what will be reported about her fate.
sentences.zh: 这为她后来的遭遇以及关于她命运的种种报道提供了一种可怕的背景。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So on the 3rd of September, which is the second day of the massacres, the killers came to a prison called La Force,
sentences.zh: 因此，在9月3日——大屠杀的第二天，行刑者来到了一个名叫拉福尔的监狱，

sentences.en: where she has been taken with the other ladies in waiting and with the royal children's former governess, Madame de Torzelle.
sentences.zh: 她和其它女侍官以及王室子女的前家庭教师德托尔泽尔夫人一起被关押在那里。

sentences.en: And there's a tribunal set up.
sentences.zh: 那里设立了一个法庭。

sentences.en: There are seven people.
sentences.zh: 有七个人。

sentences.en: The most famous of them is a radical journalist called Jacques Hébert.
sentences.zh: 其中最著名的是一个激进记者，名叫雅克·埃贝尔。

sentences.en: He basically makes Marat look like a columnist for The Guardian.
sentences.zh: 他基本上让马拉看起来就像《卫报》的专栏作家一样温和。

sentences.en: He's kind of very extreme.
sentences.zh: 他非常极端。

sentences.en: He's a bit Trump-esque, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他有点像特朗普式的风格，对吧？

sentences.en: He has nicknames for his opponents.
sentences.zh: 他会给他的政敌起外号。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Incredibly aggressive.
sentences.zh: 极具攻击性。

sentences.en: So this tribunal has been working its way through the prisoners of the force.
sentences.zh: 所以这个法庭一直在审讯那些强力部门的囚犯。

sentences.en: They have a very strange sort of code.
sentences.zh: 他们有一套非常奇怪的密码。

sentences.en: If they say at the end of your hearing, Vive la Nation, then you are spared.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在听证会结束时说“共和国万岁”，那么你就能免于一死。

sentences.en: You're free to go.
sentences.zh: 你可以重获自由。

sentences.en: If they say you're free to go, you are killed.
sentences.zh: 如果他们说你可以重获自由，那你就会被处死。

sentences.en: So it's slightly confusing.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点让人困惑。

sentences.en: Anyway, the process de Lambelle is brought out and it's all actually very quick.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，兰巴勒王妃被带了出来，整个过程其实非常快。

sentences.en: They say, did you know anything about the plot to kill the people by the Swiss guards at the Tuileries?
sentences.zh: 他们问，你知道杜伊勒里宫的瑞士卫队密谋杀害百姓的事吗？

sentences.en: So again, harking back to the sense that it's the guards who are at fault and it's a royal conspiracy against the people.
sentences.zh: 所以，这再次呼应了那种观点，即错误在于卫兵，这是一场针对人民的皇室阴谋。

sentences.en: And she says, no, I knew nothing about this.
sentences.zh: 而她说，不，我对此一无所知。

sentences.en: Will you swear to liberty and equality and hatred of the king and queen?
sentences.zh: 你愿意发誓效忠自由和平等，并宣誓痛恨国王和王后吗？

sentences.en: She says, yes, I'll happily swear to liberty and equality, but I cannot swear hatred of the king and queen.
sentences.zh: 她说，是的，我很高兴发誓效忠自由和平等，但我不能宣誓痛恨国王和王后。

sentences.en: It's not in my heart.
sentences.zh: 这违背我的内心。

sentences.en: Now, at that point, by some accounts, there was a friend or an agent of her father-in-law or something like this, who was in the room, who whispered to her, just said,
sentences.zh: 就在那时，据某些说法，房间里有她公公的朋友或特工之类的人，低声对她说，

sentences.en: say you swear it and they'll let you go.
sentences.zh: 说你发誓了，他们就会放了你。

sentences.en: And she said, I have nothing more to say.
sentences.zh: 而她说，我没什么可说的了。

sentences.en: It's indifferent to me if I die earlier or later.
sentences.zh: 我死得早一点还是晚一点，对我都一样。

sentences.en: I have made the sacrifice of my life.
sentences.zh: 我已经为我的生命做出了牺牲。

sentences.en: And the tribunal says, very well, let madame be set at liberty, which means you're for the chop.
sentences.zh: 法庭说，很好，让夫人重获自由，这意味着你要上断头台了。

sentences.en: And then she is led outside into the courtyard.
sentences.zh: 然后她被带到了外面的庭院里。

sentences.en: And now what happens next is the subject of innumerable, undoubtedly sensationalized, exaggerated and probably entirely fictional accounts.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情成为了无数毫无疑问被煽动化、夸大且可能完全虚构的叙述的主题。

sentences.en: Many of them exaggerated and many of them, frankly, probably fictional.
sentences.zh: 其中许多被夸大了，老实说，许多可能都是虚构的。

sentences.en: What do we actually know?
sentences.zh: 我们实际上知道什么？

sentences.en: What we know is that the same day, the third, a group of sans-culottes delivered her body, sans head, to one of the sections.
sentences.zh: 我们知道的是，在同一天，即三号，一群无套裤汉将她的尸体（不包括头颅）送到了其中一个区。

sentences.en: Later, the head was retrieved and these were buried privately by servants of her family.
sentences.zh: 后来，头颅被找回，并由她家族的仆人秘密埋葬。

sentences.en: That's what we actually know.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们真正知道的。

sentences.en: So we know that her head was cut off and was not there to be taken with the rest of her body to the section notary.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道她的头被砍掉了，并没有和她身体的其他部分一起被送到区公证处。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there are a couple of issues and how she was killed, which is the subject of an enormous sort of very prurient, frankly, pornographic speculation in the 1790s and afterwards.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有几个问题，关于她是如何被杀的，这在18世纪90年代及以后成为了大量非常淫秽、坦率地说是色情猜测的主题。

sentences.en: And then there is what happens to her head afterwards, which becomes a very, very famous part of the French Revolutionary story.
sentences.zh: 然后是她死后头颅的去向，这成了法国大革命故事中非常非常著名的一部分。

sentences.en: So the detail that you just mentioned about what happens to her head, which I think does happen, the story is that it gets put on a pike and it gets taken to the prison,
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到关于她头颅去向的细节，我认为确实发生了，故事说它被插在长矛上，带到了监狱里，

sentences.en: the temple fortress, where the royal family are being kept.
sentences.zh: 也就是关押王室成员的圣殿城堡。

sentences.en: And, of course, Marie Antoinette, the friend and, in the opinion of the crowd, the lesbian lover of the murdered princess.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有玛丽·安托瓦内特，这位被害公主的朋友，在群众看来，也是她的女同性恋情人。

sentences.en: And there are various accounts of what then happened.
sentences.zh: 对于接下来发生的事情有各种各样的说法。

sentences.en: Some say that Marie Antoinette looked out of the window, saw it, screamed and fainted.
sentences.zh: 有人说玛丽·安托瓦内特向窗外望去，看到了它，尖叫着昏了过去。

sentences.en: This seems an exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 这似乎有些夸大其词。

sentences.en: The likelihood is that she didn't see it.
sentences.zh: 可能性是她根本没看到。

sentences.en: She wasn't actually there at the time.
sentences.zh: 她当时其实不在那里。

sentences.en: I think she wasn't in the room.
sentences.zh: 我认为她不在房间里。

sentences.en: There's a story that the governor of the prison's wife sees it and faints and people thought that was Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 有个说法是监狱长的妻子看到了并昏了过去，而人们以为那是玛丽·安托瓦内特。

sentences.en: I think it's possible they put the head on the pike, by the way, to the temple prison.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我认为他们把头挂在长矛上带到圣殿监狱是有可能的。

sentences.en: I think that sounds like something they might have done.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这听起来像是他们会做的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意。

sentences.en: And I think that, as we'll probably explore later in the episode, it's partly because parading heads on pikes has become a part of revolutionary justice.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，正如我们稍后在本集节目中可能探讨的那样，部分原因是在长矛上游街示众已经成为革命审判的一部分。

sentences.en: So the beheading of enemies of the revolution, the parading of their heads, this is part of the language of justice on the streets.
sentences.zh: 因此，对革命敌人的斩首，对他们头颅的游街示众，这是街头正义语言的一部分。

sentences.en: So you would almost expect that to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以你几乎会预料到这种事发生。

sentences.en: There's also, there's a terrible story about the Duke of Orléans, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 还有一个，关于奥尔良公爵的可怕故事，对吧？

sentences.en: As it was, who's now become Philippe Egalité.
sentences.zh: 也就是现在成为平等菲利普的那个人。

sentences.en: One of the worst people who's ever lived.
sentences.zh: 有史以来最糟糕的人之一。

sentences.en: But again, I don't believe this story.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我不相信这个故事。

sentences.en: There's a story that he's at the Palais Royale and he's having dinner with some English friends, English guests.
sentences.zh: 有个故事说他在皇家宫殿与一些英国朋友、英国客人共进晚餐。

sentences.en: And somebody brings in the heads and he looks at him and he says, oh, that's Lombard.
sentences.zh: 有人把头颅拿进来，他看了一眼说，哦，那是隆巴尔。

sentences.en: I know her by her long hair.
sentences.zh: 我从她长长的头发认得她。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's have, let's have dinner.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们吃饭吧。

sentences.en: Again, I don't think that happened.
sentences.zh: 同样，我认为那没有发生。

sentences.en: I think he's such a terrible man that I'd like to believe it did happen.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是个如此糟糕的人，以至于我倒挺希望这是真的。

sentences.en: It reflects very badly on him.
sentences.zh: 这极大地反映了他的败坏。

sentences.en: I mean, the question of whether the stories are true and won't go into all the details, but there is one particularly notorious account of what happened that I'm going to quote.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些故事是否属实的问题，我们不会探讨所有细节，但有一个特别恶劣的关于发生什么的叙述我要引用。

sentences.en: And anyone listening who maybe has children or who doesn't want to hear it, just block out the next couple of minutes.
sentences.zh: 任何在听的听众，如果可能带着孩子或者不想听，请屏蔽接下来的几分钟。

sentences.en: But this is a detail that was reported by a playwright.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个由剧作家报道的细节。

sentences.en: And again, it's intriguing how often playwrights and fiction writers crop up in these stories.
sentences.zh: 同样，引人注目的是，剧作家和小说家在这些故事中出现得是多么频繁。

sentences.en: He'd been sympathetic to the revolution.
sentences.zh: 他曾同情过革命。

sentences.en: But seven years on, when he wrote this, he turned radically against it, become a counter-revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 但七年后，当他写下这些时，他彻底反对革命，成了一个反革命分子。

sentences.en: He's a man called Louis-Sébastien Mercier.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫路易-塞巴斯蒂安·梅尔西耶。

sentences.en: And he wrote, when the Princess de Lombard was mutilated in a hundred different ways.
sentences.zh: 他写道，当隆巴尔王妃以一百种不同的方式遭受残害时。

sentences.en: So already there we have, you know, the escalation of the kind of torture porn, if you like.
sentences.zh: 所以在那儿我们已经看到了，你知道的，这种虐待色情的升级，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: And the murderers had partaken of the bleeding morsels of her corpse.
sentences.zh: 凶手们分享了她尸体上还在流血的碎块。

sentences.en: So he's saying they're eating her.
sentences.zh: 所以他是说他们在吃她。

sentences.en: I mean, the charge of cannibalism there is being overt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那里的食人指控是公开的。

sentences.en: But one of the monsters cut off her virginal part and made it into a moustache.
sentences.zh: 但其中一个恶魔切下了她处女的部位，把它做成了胡子。

sentences.en: And the reason for quoting this specifically,
sentences.zh: 而具体引用这一点的原因，

sentences.en: partly it reflects the way in which counter-revolutionaries are drawing on the kind of the libertine pornography of which the Marquis de Sade is the exemplar.
sentences.zh: 部分是因为它反映了反革命分子正在利用萨德侯爵作为典范的那种浪荡色情制品。

sentences.en: But it also, I think, points to one of the ways in which the September massacres will be understood and have been understood,
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，它指出了九月大屠将被理解和已经被理解的方式之一，

sentences.en: which is as an efflorescence of literal demons from hell, monsters who have lost all trace of humanity and can perpetrate the most revolting atrocities.
sentences.zh: 即把它视为地狱中字面上的恶魔的涌现，是那些丧失了所有人性痕迹并能犯下最令人作呕暴行的怪物。

sentences.en: And this will be a way in which, in the wake of the revolution, throughout the 19th into the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 这将成为一种方式，在大革命之后，贯穿19世纪到20世纪，

sentences.en: counter-revolutionary traditions in France and beyond will interpret the September massacres as being not a kind of clinical, patient,
sentences.zh: 法国及其他地方的反革命传统将把九月大屠杀解释为，不是一种临床的、耐心的、有条不紊地消灭他们视为罪犯的人的行为，

sentences.en: methodical elimination of people who they see as criminals, but as an orgy of destruction and murder.
sentences.zh: 而是一场毁灭和谋杀的狂欢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's the stuff of a Gil Ray cartoon.
sentences.zh: 那是吉尔雷漫画的题材。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So my take on this is these stories are incredibly controversial among historians.
sentences.zh: 所以我对此的看法是，这些故事在历史学家中极具争议。

sentences.en: And as we will see, because we'll get into that in a little while, my view is a lot of these stories are clearly made up.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，因为我们稍后会深入探讨，我的观点是，许多这些故事显然是编造的。

sentences.en: You know, the stories of the most grotesque torture, the stories of cannibalism, people drinking blood, all of that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些最怪诞的酷刑故事，食人的故事，人们喝血的故事，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: It's part of a tradition of kind of political invective to invent these stories.
sentences.zh: 这是编造这些故事的政治抨击传统的一部分。

sentences.en: But I think it's implausible to imagine that a thousand people were killed without, as it were, people overstepping the mark.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，想象一千人被杀而没有哪怕可以说是人们越界的情况，是不合情理的。

sentences.en: You know, without mutilation, without rape.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，没有残害，没有强奸。

sentences.en: Because there were suggestions that some of the prostitutes, for example.
sentences.zh: 因为有迹象表明，例如，一些妓女。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In the suffrage, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 在选举权中，对，对。

sentences.en: Were abused or raped.
sentences.zh: 被虐待或强奸。

sentences.en: Is that inherently implausible?
sentences.zh: 这本质上是不合情理的吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: I think a lot of these, these are horrific killing.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中很多，这些都是可怕的杀戮。

sentences.en: They're not entirely surgical.
sentences.zh: 它们并非完全是外科手术般的精准。

sentences.en: However, I do agree with you that a mad frenzy is the wrong way to think about it.
sentences.zh: 然而，我确实同意你的看法，即把这视为疯狂的狂热是错误的看法。

sentences.en: That it is pretty clear from a lot of these accounts, like that account that we quoted before the break of that guy who let go.
sentences.zh: 从许多这些叙述中可以相当清楚地看出，就像我们在中场休息前引用的那个放走人的家伙的叙述一样。

sentences.en: There is a kind of semblance of justice.
sentences.zh: 这里有一种正义的表象。

sentences.en: We know that the killers took these tribunals.
sentences.zh: 我们知道凶手们进行了这些审判。

sentences.en: That they're not all just sort of dancing around, wearing people's body parts as hats or whatever, covered in blood.
sentences.zh: 他们并不只是到处载歌载舞，戴着别人的身体部位当帽子或者浑身是血。

sentences.en: That they are actually trying to take these tribunals quite seriously.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是在试图非常认真地对待这些审判。

sentences.en: We know that the crowds listened to the evidence.
sentences.zh: 我们知道群众倾听了证据。

sentences.en: And we do know that the killings were carried out in silence because so many people talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道杀戮是在沉默中进行的，因为有太多人谈到这一点。

sentences.en: Somber, somber.
sentences.zh: 阴郁，阴郁。

sentences.en: Solemn.
sentences.zh: 庄严。

sentences.en: Yeah, solemn atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 是的，庄严的氛围。

sentences.en: I mean, some people have talked about it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人谈到过这一点。

sentences.en: They've said it was almost like they were ritualistic killings.
sentences.zh: 他们说这几乎就像是仪式性的杀戮。

sentences.en: That there was a kind of, dare I say to them, I don't want to give you a massive gift, but it's kind of sacral dimension to it.
sentences.zh: 有一种，我敢对他们说吗，我不想给你送上一份厚礼，但这其中有一种神圣的维度。

sentences.en: That it was a purge.
sentences.zh: 这是一场清洗。

sentences.en: It was a kind of purge of sin.
sentences.zh: 这是一种对罪恶的清洗。

sentences.en: So it's often said, I think correctly, that there is a presaging here of the notion of cleansing a state of disease that we see in the 20th century totalitarian states.
sentences.zh: 所以人们经常说，我认为这是正确的，这里预示着我们在20世纪极权主义国家中看到的净化国家疾病的概念。

sentences.en: Whether it's the fascists or the communists.
sentences.zh: 无论是法西斯主义者还是共产主义者。

sentences.en: But I genuinely think it is also drawing on those Christian traditions.
sentences.zh: 但我真心认为它也在借鉴这些基督教传统。

sentences.en: Because you talked about a holocauSt.
sentences.zh: 因为你谈到了大屠杀。

sentences.en: The holocaust is a burnt offering to the gods.
sentences.zh: 大屠杀是对神明的烧烤供奉。

sentences.en: That's originally what it was.
sentences.zh: 这最初就是它的意思。

sentences.en: Transmuted into a Christian context.
sentences.zh: 转化为基督教的语境。

sentences.en: Because these are all happening in abbeys.
sentences.zh: 因为这些都发生在修道院里。

sentences.en: In convents.
sentences.zh: 在女修道院里。

sentences.en: And the sense the inquisitors had that they were doing God's work when they burn the diseased limb of the tree.
sentences.zh: 以及宗教裁判所人员觉得他们在烧毁树木生病的枝桠时是在替上帝行事的信念。

sentences.en: This is very similar to the language that you were having with the September massacres.
sentences.zh: 这与你在九月大屠杀中所使用的语言非常相似。

sentences.en: And I think that, I mean, I agree.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我的意思是，我同意。

sentences.en: I'm sure that there must have been some kind of sexual sadism going on, maybe particularly at the Salpetrier.
sentences.zh: 我确信当时一定发生了一些某种程度的性虐待狂，也许特别是在萨尔佩特里埃。

sentences.en: But just to say, on that issue, it's a Salpetrier where the fewest prisoners are killed.
sentences.zh: 但只想说明一点，在萨尔佩特里埃，被杀的囚犯是最少的。

sentences.en: I think it's something like 40, did we say?
sentences.zh: 我想大概是40人，我们是这么说的吗？

sentences.en: But there are 280 or 90 there.
sentences.zh: 但那里有280或290人。

sentences.en: So, relatively speaking, I mean, it's not like they're breaking into a prison full of prostitutes and going mad in the way that rakes in a Sard novel would.
sentences.zh: 所以，相对而言，我的意思是，这不像他们闯入一个满是妓女的监狱并像萨德小说中的浪荡公子那样发疯。

sentences.en: So, I think that is, for me, the most chilling thing about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为，对我来说，这是其中最令人不寒栗的事情。

sentences.en: It is murder done in the cause of virtue.
sentences.zh: 这是以美德之名进行的谋杀。

sentences.en: Oh, I totally agree with that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我完全同意这一点。

sentences.en: I think that the people who do it think they're doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为实施这些的人认为他们在做正确的事。

sentences.en: They think it's a necessary purge.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一场必要的清洗。

sentences.en: But that is also why it's important for counter-revolutionary propagandists to frame it as pornographic,
sentences.zh: 但这也是为什么反革命宣传家必须把它框定为色情的原因，

sentences.en: because that undermines the claim of those who perpetrated these executions to be virtuous.
sentences.zh: 因为这破坏了那些犯下这些处决的人自称是美德的声称。

sentences.en: I think, actually, the pornographic kind of mode is the one that people instinctively reach for, because Paris is awash with it.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我认为色情这种模式是人们本能会想到的，因为巴黎到处都是这种东西。

sentences.en: I think it's the natural genre to pick.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是自然而然会选择的流派。

sentences.en: But I think it is natural for those who repudiate the notion that this has anything to do with virtue.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，对于那些否认这与美德有任何关系的人来说，这是很自然的。

sentences.en: Okay, let's just sum up the story.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们来总结一下这个故事。

sentences.en: So, it takes four days.
sentences.zh: 所以，这持续了四天。

sentences.en: The massacres in the prisons last for four days.
sentences.zh: 监狱里的大屠杀持续了四天。

sentences.en: They die down on the morning of the 6th of September.
sentences.zh: 它们在9月6日早晨平息下来。

sentences.en: To give you a sense of what Paris looks like, the place is absolutely full of bodies.
sentences.zh: 为了让你对巴黎的面貌有个概念，这个地方到处都是尸体。

sentences.en: There are bodies in the streets.
sentences.zh: 街上有尸体。

sentences.en: There are bodies in the courtyards.
sentences.zh: 庭院里有尸体。

sentences.en: There are bodies in the kind of corridors of the prison.
sentences.zh: 监狱的走廊里有尸体。

sentences.en: The rest of the prisoners, of course, have been set free.
sentences.zh: 当然，其余的囚犯都已经被释放了。

sentences.en: So, the prison's empty.
sentences.zh: 所以，监狱空了。

sentences.en: And the commune eventually sends in people and says, please scrub them down and wash them with vinegar.
sentences.zh: 最终，公社派人去把他们冲洗干净，用醋清洗。

sentences.en: Get rid of the stench.
sentences.zh: 清除恶臭。

sentences.en: Get rid of the stains.
sentences.zh: 洗掉血迹。

sentences.en: But in some of the prisons, La Force, for example, there's so much blood they can't shift the bloodstains.
sentences.zh: 但在某些监狱里，比如拉福尔监狱，血迹实在太多，他们根本无法清理。

sentences.en: Of course, a Tom Holland would say, some of the rooms are stained with blood, but some of them are pristine and perfectly clean.
sentences.zh: 当然，像汤姆·霍兰这样的人会说，有些房间沾满了血，但也有一些房间一尘不染、完美干净。

sentences.en: Why not talk about those rooms?
sentences.zh: 为什么不谈谈那些房间呢？

sentences.en: Anyway, we'll get into this in a second, Tom, because we're going to talk about the historiography.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，汤姆，我们一会儿再讨论这个，因为我们要聊聊史学史。

sentences.en: There are copycat killings elsewhere in France.
sentences.zh: 法国其他地方也发生了模仿杀戮。

sentences.en: So, there are 44 people, for example, that are killed in Versailles.
sentences.zh: 例如，凡尔赛有44人被杀。

sentences.en: A horrendous atrocity, actually.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一场骇人听闻的暴行。

sentences.en: They are lynched.
sentences.zh: 他们被私刑处死。

sentences.en: They are beheaded in public.
sentences.zh: 他们在公众场合被斩首。

sentences.en: And their heads are stuck on the spikes of the palace gates.
sentences.zh: 他们的头颅被插在宫殿大门的尖桩上。

sentences.en: So, probably about 100 people are killed across France.
sentences.zh: 所以，整个法国大约有100人被杀。

sentences.en: But then, in the next few weeks, things die down.
sentences.zh: 但随后，在接下来的几周里，局势平息了下来。

sentences.en: And in the future episodes, we'll talk about why that happens.
sentences.zh: 在未来的节目中，我们将探讨为什么会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: The political transformation in Paris.
sentences.zh: 巴黎的政治转型。

sentences.en: And a very dramatic change on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 以及战场上的戏剧性巨变。

sentences.en: Just to move towards a close on the September massacres.
sentences.zh: 为了给九月大屠杀划上一个段落。

sentences.en: One question is, what did people in Paris think of them?
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题是，巴黎人对它们是怎么看的？

sentences.en: And we know people in Paris thought they were fine.
sentences.zh: 我们知道巴黎人觉得这没什么问题。

sentences.en: They were completely fine.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得完全没问题。

sentences.en: David Andrus, who you've mentioned before, he makes a very good point that Parisians are used to public violence.
sentences.zh: 你之前提到过的大卫·安德鲁斯提出了一个很好的观点，巴黎人已经习惯了公开暴力。

sentences.en: I mean, you talked about it, Tom, in that excellent episode you did on the guillotine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，你在那期关于断头台的精彩节目中谈到过这个。

sentences.en: The hideous rituals of the public executions.
sentences.zh: 公开处决的骇人仪式。

sentences.en: The idea of humiliating, degrading, and destroying somebody in public.
sentences.zh: 在公开场合羞辱、贬低和摧毁一个人。

sentences.en: But Dominic, also what we talked about in that episode was how the revolution equates itself with humanitarian impulses.
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，我们在那期节目中讨论的还有，革命如何将自身与人道主义冲动等同起来。

sentences.en: And it may seem mad to talk about humanitarian impulses in the context of the September massacres.
sentences.zh: 在九月大屠杀的背景下谈论人道主义冲动似乎很疯狂。

sentences.en: But I suspect that, I mean,
sentences.zh: 但我怀疑，我的意思是，

sentences.en: maybe a majority of the people doing the executions would say that actually they're not kind of publicly tearing people apart with horses or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 也许大多数执行处决的人会说，实际上他们并没有用马把人活活扯碎之类的事情。

sentences.en: They're doing it expeditiously.
sentences.zh: 他们行动迅速。

sentences.en: And the whole tradition of hanging people from lanterns and then parading their heads is seen as revolutionary justice, but is already starting to be phased out.
sentences.zh: 把人挂在路灯上然后游街示众的传统被视为革命正义，但已经开始逐步淘汰了。

sentences.en: It's clearly a cause of embarrassment for the revolutionary authorities.
sentences.zh: 这显然让革命当局感到尴尬。

sentences.en: And that is why, exactly as this is going on, the guillotine is starting to be introduced and is becoming more and more the emblem of how criminals should be dispatched.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，就在这一切发生的同时，断头台开始被引入，并越来越成为如何处置罪犯的象征。

sentences.en: And the September massacres, I'm sure, must play a key role in that process.
sentences.zh: 我确信，九月大屠杀在这个过程中扮演了关键角色。

sentences.en: The people in the revolutionary authorities think, OK, fine, I mean, it's cruel necessity, but it would be better to do it with the guillotine.
sentences.zh: 革命当局的人心想，好吧，这虽然是残酷的必需，但用断头台来做会更好。

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting that the papers at the time, they're not embarrassed about it at all.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当时的报纸对此一点也不感到尴尬。

sentences.en: This is a moderate paper, the Courrier Francais.
sentences.zh: 这是一份温派报纸，《法兰西信使》。

sentences.en: The people made it their duty to purge the city of all the criminals to prevent a prison breakout that would have fallen on the women and children.
sentences.zh: 人民把清除城中所有罪犯当作自己的责任，以防止可能波及妇女和儿童的越狱事件。

sentences.en: More radical paper, Révolution de Paris.
sentences.zh: 更激进的报纸，《巴黎革命报》。

sentences.en: The people took the extreme measure, but the only appropriate one,
sentences.zh: 人民采取了极端但唯一恰当的措施，

sentences.en: of forestalling the horrors that were being prepared against them and of showing no mercy to those who would not have shown any to them.
sentences.zh: 来阻止针对他们的恐怖阴谋，对那些不会对他们手软的人毫不留情。

sentences.en: But if you have a machine that can just slice a head off, you don't need courtyards full of peoples with butcher's knives.
sentences.zh: 但如果你有一台能直接切下脑袋的机器，你就不需要满院子拿着屠夫刀具的人了。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, we have diarists, we have letter writers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们有日记作者，我们有书信作者。

sentences.en: There's a brilliant example of a guy, a merchant's son, an 18-year-old in Peter McPhee's book on the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 彼得·麦克菲关于法国大革命的书里有一个出色的例子，讲的是一个年轻人，一个商人的儿子，18岁。

sentences.en: And he wrote home and he said, there has been a horrible massacre.
sentences.zh: 他写信回家说，发生了一场可怕的大屠杀。

sentences.en: He says, wherever you go, you see the bloody remains of mutilated bodies in open graves.
sentences.zh: 他说，无论你走到哪里，都能在开挖的坟墓里看到残缺尸体的血腥遗骸。

sentences.en: And then in the next line, he says, but it was the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 接着在下一行，他说，但这确实是正确的事。

sentences.en: The prisoners were plotting with the Prussians.
sentences.zh: 囚犯们在与普鲁士人勾结。

sentences.en: We had to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不这么做。

sentences.en: And that diarist, Rosalie Julien, she said, again, an atrocious necessity.
sentences.zh: 那个日记作者罗莎莉·朱利安也说过，又是一次残酷的必需。

sentences.en: The people, terrible in their fury, are avenging the crimes of three years of vile treachery.
sentences.zh: 人民在愤怒中极其可怕，正在为三年邪恶背叛的罪行复仇。

sentences.en: And she talks in her diary.
sentences.zh: 她在日记里写道。

sentences.en: She says, people have had their heads cut off.
sentences.zh: 她说，有人被砍了头。

sentences.en: Priests have been eviscerated.
sentences.zh: 神甫被剖腹。

sentences.en: But it's the right thing to do because, you know, we had to save France.
sentences.zh: 但这做得很对，因为你知道，我们必须拯救法国。

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, historians have grappled with this ever since.
sentences.zh: 问题是，历史学家们从此一直缠斗于此。

sentences.en: Because, of course, most historians, by and large, I would say, who write about the French Revolution, especially in France, have been sympathetic to the revolution.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，大多数撰写法国大革命历史的历史学家，尤其是法国的历史学家，大体上都对革命抱有同情。

sentences.en: And here you have an episode which is, for me, much more shocking than the terror.
sentences.zh: 而这里发生了一场对我来说比恐怖统治更令人震惊的事件。

sentences.en: I mean, the victims and the terror, a lot of them are people involved in politics, players in the games.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，恐怖统治中的受害者，很多都是卷入政治的人，是局中人。

sentences.en: They're players.
sentences.zh: 他们是玩家。

sentences.en: These people are often young, very poor, the criminals, the petty thieves, the women, the prostitutes, the prince de Lambat.
sentences.zh: 而这些人通常很年轻，非常贫困，是罪犯、小偷、妇女、妓女、朗巴尔亲王夫人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, from the 21st century perspective, I know Theo says, oh, you're always harder on French exponents of violence than you are when the British do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，从21世纪的角度来看，我知道西奥说，哦，你对法国的暴力行为总是比英国人这样做时更严厉。

sentences.en: But I think even with that said, it's hard to contemplate this and to say, oh, yeah, they had to go, as Theo clearly thinks.
sentences.zh: 但即使这样说，也很难去审视这一点然后说，哦，是的，他们活该，西奥显然是这么认为的。

sentences.en: I think you're being a bit harsh on Theo there.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你对西奥有点太严厉了。

sentences.en: You say that it's not comparable to the terror.
sentences.zh: 你说这与恐怖统治没有可比性。

sentences.en: I mean, lots of innocent people die in the terror.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在恐怖统治中有大量无辜的人死去。

sentences.en: And the difference is that death by the guillotine is more clinical than being hacked to death by people armed with knives and choppers.
sentences.zh: 区别在于，死于断头台比被手持刀具和砍刀的人乱刀砍死要更具医疗般的冷酷。

sentences.en: Don't you think?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I probably would choose the guillotine over being hacked to death by a carpenter with a saw.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比起被一个拿着锯子的木匠乱刀砍死，我大概会选择断头台。

sentences.en: At one o'clock in the morning?
sentences.zh: 在凌晨一点？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the definitive French historian of this was a guy called Pierre Caron, and he was writing in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 关于这段历史的权威法国历史学家是一个名叫皮埃尔·卡隆的人，他在20世纪30年代写作。

sentences.en: He was the head of the National Archives in France.
sentences.zh: 他是法国国家档案馆的馆长。

sentences.en: And he said, you have to understand it in the context of two things.
sentences.zh: 他说，你必须在两个背景下去理解它。

sentences.en: One, the fighting at the Tuileries and the thirst for vengeance.
sentences.zh: 第一，杜伊勒里宫的战斗和对复仇的渴望。

sentences.en: And the other is the mood of panic and hysteria as the Prussians advanced on the capital.
sentences.zh: 第二，当普鲁士人推进到首都时那种恐慌和歇斯底里的情绪。

sentences.en: And that you have to understand, you know, the war, the pressure and all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你必须理解战争、压力以及所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And Caron, for years, everybody said, he's the top man in the September massacres.
sentences.zh: 多年来，所有人对卡隆的评价都是，他是九月大屠杀研究的顶级专家。

sentences.en: He knows what's what.
sentences.zh: 他什么都懂。

sentences.en: And then 50 years later, our old friend Simon Sharma wrote his book Citizens.
sentences.zh: 然后50年过去了，我们的老朋友西蒙·沙玛写了他的书《公民们》。

sentences.en: Have you read the passage where he talks about Caron?
sentences.zh: 你读过他谈论卡隆的那段话吗？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 我读过。

sentences.en: He says his book is, and I quote, a monument of intellectual cowardice and moral self-delusion.
sentences.zh: 他说他的书是，我引用一下，“知识分子的怯懦和道德自我欺骗的丰碑”。

sentences.en: And he said, Caron is being far too kind.
sentences.zh: 他说，卡隆实在是太仁慈了。

sentences.en: This is basically anticipating the genocides of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是在预示20世纪的种族灭绝。

sentences.en: The same themes.
sentences.zh: 同样的主题。

sentences.en: We have to get them before they get us.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在他们对付我们之前先对付他们。

sentences.en: The same emphasis on a kind of what Sharma calls an armed sanitation.
sentences.zh: 同样强调沙玛所称的武装净化。

sentences.en: On purging France of crime and sin.
sentences.zh: 清除法国的犯罪和罪恶。

sentences.en: And you can see why Sharma, writing in the 1980s, very conscious of what had happened in Europe 40 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解为什么在20世纪80年代写作的沙玛，对40年前欧洲发生的事情有着深刻的感知。

sentences.en: Why he looks at September massacres and says, hey, don't make excuses for this.
sentences.zh: 为什么他看到九月大屠杀时会说，嘿，不要为这找借口。

sentences.en: This is unbelievably horrible and bestial.
sentences.zh: 这是难以置信的恐怖和野蛮。

sentences.en: And he doesn't deny that there's a kind of efficiency and a clinical nature to it.
sentences.zh: 他不否认其中有一种效率和临床般的冷酷。

sentences.en: But he says that's what makes it all the more frightening.
sentences.zh: 但他认为，正因如此它才更加让人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: But equally, he literally is repeating counter-revolutionary propaganda.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，他实际上是在重复反革命的宣传。

sentences.en: So to quote him from Citizens when he's writing about Caron, some accounts, including that of Mercier,
sentences.zh: 因此，引用他在《公民们》中写到卡隆的话，一些记述，包括梅西耶的记述——

sentences.en: so that's the playwright whose account of the fate of the Prince of Lombard we quoted, insist on the obscene mutilation and the display of her genitals.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们引用过的那个关于朗巴尔亲王夫人命运的剧作家——坚持声称存在淫秽的尸体损毁以及对其生殖器的展示。

sentences.en: A story which Caron dismisses with the cloistered certainty of the archivist as intrinsically inconceivable.
sentences.zh: 卡隆带着档案保管员那深居简出的确定性，将这个故事作为本质上不可想象的内容予以驳回。

sentences.en: But we know that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道那并没有发生。

sentences.en: And we know that because of research that has happened since he wrote Citizens.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道，是因为在他写完《公民们》之后开展的研究。

sentences.en: So French historian Antoine de Back,
sentences.zh: 法国历史学家安托万·德巴克，

sentences.en: he's the guy who went through all the records of the sections and found that the body of the Prince of Lombard was given to the notary of the local section.
sentences.zh: 就是那个翻遍了各区档案、发现朗巴尔亲王夫人的尸体被交给了当地区的公证员的人。

sentences.en: And he recorded what had happened and none of these mutilations had happened.
sentences.zh: 他记录了发生的事情，根本没有发生过任何这些肢解。

sentences.en: So we know for a fact that that is counter-revolutionary propaganda.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以确定那是反革命宣传。

sentences.en: And that when Caron dismisses it, it's not because he's some cloistered archivist, but because actually he's right about that.
sentences.zh: 当卡隆驳斥它时，并不是因为他是什么深居简出的档案管理员，而是因为他在这一点上确实是对的。

sentences.en: That wasn't happening.
sentences.zh: 那种事根本没发生。

sentences.en: So in this case, right, I agree with you, it didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，对吧，我同意你的看法，这并没有发生。

sentences.en: The thing is, do you take all the revolutionary sources on trust and say the counter-revolutionary ones are propagandistic exaggerations?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你是盲目相信所有的革命信源，并认为反革命信源是宣传性的夸大吗？

sentences.en: Or do you say that the truth probably lies in between the two and that both of them are party pre?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为真相可能介于两者之间，并且双方都带有党派偏见？

sentences.en: And actually, the truth is that we'll never really know.
sentences.zh: 实际上，真相是我们永远无法真正知晓。

sentences.en: And this is the frustrating thing about this story.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个故事令人沮丧的地方。

sentences.en: It's a classic example of historians projecting onto it their own political preconception.
sentences.zh: 这是历史学家将他们自己的政治先入为主强加于之上的典型例子。

sentences.en: So you give these, we talked about David Andrus.
sentences.zh: 所以你举了这些例子，我们谈到了大卫·安德鲁斯。

sentences.en: David Andrus is very much a man of the left.
sentences.zh: 大卫·安德鲁斯是非常典型的左翼人士。

sentences.en: In his book on the terror, you know, he says the September massacres are terrible.
sentences.zh: 在他的恐怖统治著作中，你知道，他说九月大屠杀是可怕的。

sentences.en: But then in the next breath, he has a sentence like this.
sentences.zh: 但转头在下一句，他写下了这样一句话。

sentences.en: This is where he introduces the September massacres.
sentences.zh: 这就是他引入九月大屠杀的地方。

sentences.en: The people in arms exercised their right of self-defense against those they felt were betraying them to the counter-revolution.
sentences.zh: 武装的人民行使了自卫权，去对付那些他们觉得正在向反革命出卖自己的人。

sentences.en: You cannot imagine Simon Sharma writing that sentence, can you?
sentences.zh: 你无法想象西蒙·沙玛会写出那句话，对吧？

sentences.en: David No, you can't.
sentences.zh: 大卫，不，你想象不到。

sentences.en: But I think that's slightly to misrepresent what he's saying.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这稍微曲解了他的意思。

sentences.en: I mean, he is saying that that is precisely the horror.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是在说，这恰恰是恐怖之处。

sentences.en: You know, they think that they're doing justice, and that is precisely why it is terrifying.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们认为自己在主持正义，而这正是它令人毛骨悚然的原因。

sentences.en: You know, he's saying, I guess in the way that a Christian would say about what the Inquisition did, and I think that there is an absolute continuity there, as I've said,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他说的话，我想就像一个基督徒对宗教裁判所所作所为的评价一样，我认为那里存在着绝对的延续性，正如我所说的那样，

sentences.en: that it's the realization that you can launch a pogrom, execute people in cold blood, and feel that you are doing it in the cause of what is right.
sentences.zh: 那就是你意识到你可以发起一场大屠杀，冷血地处决他人，并觉得你是在为正义事业而战。

sentences.en: That's what's frightening.
sentences.zh: 这才是最可怕的地方。

sentences.en: David Yeah, but I don't think that excuses it.
sentences.zh: 大卫，是的，但我不认为这可以作为借口。

sentences.en: I think that makes it all the more terrifying.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让它变得更加令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: David No, but I don't think David Andrus thinks that either.
sentences.zh: 大卫，不，但我不认为大卫·安德鲁斯也是这么想的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that I'm no expert in the historiography of the French Revolution, but the reading I've done of writers who are on the left about this
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，虽然我不是法国大革命史学方面的专家，但我读过的左翼作家关于这方面的作品

sentences.en: is that they do acknowledge that that is what is frightening.
sentences.zh: 表明，他们确实承认这正是令人恐惧的地方。

sentences.en: David Yeah.
sentences.zh: 大卫，是的。

sentences.en: David You can commit atrocities and feel that you're doing it in the cause of right.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你可以犯下暴行，却觉得你是在为正义事业而战。

sentences.en: And as I say, it's like a Christian having to face up to, you know, the executions that have been done in the name of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这就像一个基督徒不得不正视，你知道的，那些以基督之名进行的处决。

sentences.en: David Well, are you not the person who did an episode about how the Nazis thought what they were doing was right, and they were on the right side of history,
sentences.zh: 大卫，好吧，难道不是你做了一期节目，讲述纳粹如何认为他们所做的事情是正确的，他们站在历史正确的一边，

sentences.en: and on the right side of kind of morality?
sentences.zh: 并且站在某种道德正确的一边吗？

sentences.en: David Yes, and that's where the analogy, I suppose Sharma's point about the sanitation, kicks in.
sentences.zh: 大卫，是的，这就是类比的切入点，我想沙玛关于净化的观点就是从这里开始的。

sentences.en: David It's absolutely the right one.
sentences.zh: 大卫，这绝对是正确的。

sentences.en: So there's another brilliant story.
sentences.zh: 所以还有另一个精彩的故事。

sentences.en: David It's a book on the French Revolution, the most recent English language survey.
sentences.zh: 大卫，这是一本关于法国大革命的书，是最近的一部英文综合著作。

sentences.en: It's by a guy called Jeremy Popke, an American historian, professor at the University of Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 作者是一个叫杰里米·波普金的人，他是美国历史学家、肯塔基大学教授。

sentences.en: And he is much more positive about the revolution than Sharma is.
sentences.zh: 他对革命的看法比沙玛要积极得多。

sentences.en: And he says in his section on this, he says, listen, if you think the French Revolution is better than the experiments of the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 他在关于这部分的章节里说，听着，如果你认为法国大革命比20世纪的试验更好，

sentences.en: for example, communism, or indeed, Nazism, if you think the French Revolution is more progressive, as he clearly does,
sentences.zh: 例如共产主义，或者纳粹主义，如果你认为法国大革命更具进步性，就像他显然认为的那样，

sentences.en: he says, you should have a massive problem with the September massacres.
sentences.zh: 他说，你对九月大屠杀应该会有巨大的困惑。

sentences.en: Because he says, the thing that is so frightening about them is that they are so cold-bloodedly
sentences.zh: 因为他说，关于它们最可怕的事情在于它们是如此冷血

sentences.en: political, that they are people sitting down in committee rooms and saying, yeah, these people have got to go.
sentences.zh: 政治化的，是人们坐在委员会的房间里说，对，这些人必须走。

sentences.en: Go ahead and do it.
sentences.zh: 去做吧。

sentences.en: Somebody organized the death squads.
sentences.zh: 有人组织了行刑队。

sentences.en: I mean, of course, they were bottom-up to some degree, but there were people who led them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，它们在某种程度上是自下而上的，但有人领导了它们。

sentences.en: There were people who condoned it.
sentences.zh: 有人默许了这一点。

sentences.en: There were people who didn't intervene, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 有人没有进行干涉，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And his version, and indeed, Timothy Tackett and other historians, they say this is a key step towards what we call the reign of terror.
sentences.zh: 他的看法，以及蒂莫西·塔凯特和其他历史学家，都认为这是通往我们所称的恐怖统治的关键一步。

sentences.en: You know, the idea that you, maybe you'll make some mistakes and some innocent people will be
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种想法是，也许你会犯一些错误，一些无辜的人会

sentences.en: rounded up and killed accidentally, but it's actually better to purge than to allow the evil, as they see it, to fester in your midSt.
sentences.zh: 被无意中抓捕并杀害，但实际上，与其让邪恶在你们中间滋生，不如进行清洗。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: And that is, I think, what is frightening about it.
sentences.zh: 我想，这正是它令人恐惧的地方。

sentences.en: But I think that historians of all political persuasions would now see that as being what's frightening about it, I think.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，各种政治倾向的历史学家现在都会认为这正是它可怕的地方。

sentences.en: Well, because obviously we're going to be talking about this an awful lot when we get the terror itself, but let's not get ahead of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 好吧，因为很显然，当我们真正谈到恐怖统治时，我们会大量讨论这一点，但我们不要操之过急。

sentences.en: The elections to the National Convention have been happening all this time, and all the big names are standing.
sentences.zh: 国民公会的选举一直在进行，所有大人物都在参选。

sentences.en: Brissot, Robespierre, Danton, Marat.
sentences.zh: 布里索、罗伯斯庇尔、丹东、马拉。

sentences.en: This new convention is going to meet on the 20th of September, and it is going to decide
sentences.zh: 这个新的国民公会将於9月20日开会，并将决定

sentences.en: the future of France, and in particular, something I know you'll be talking about in a couple of episodes' time, the future of the royal family.
sentences.zh: 法国的未来，特别是，我知道你们将在接下来的几集里讨论的王室的未来。

sentences.en: But the question is, will this convention even get the chance to do that?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这个国民公会甚至有机会这样做吗？

sentences.en: Because all this time, the Prussians have been coming closer and closer and closer.
sentences.zh: 因为一直以来，普鲁士军队越来越近了。

sentences.en: So Verdun fell, the Duke of Brunswick, is coming on.
sentences.zh: 凡尔登沦陷了，不伦瑞克公爵正在逼近。

sentences.en: He's got 80,000 men every day.
sentences.zh: 他每天带着8万大军。

sentences.en: He is coming closer to Paris.
sentences.zh: 他正在逼近巴黎。

sentences.en: He is now being pursued by a smaller French army under General Dumouriez, who is the foreign minister who got France into the war in the first place.
sentences.zh: 他现在正被迪穆里埃将军率领的一支较小的法军追赶，迪穆里埃就是那个最初把法国拖入战争的外交大臣。

sentences.en: And by the third week in September, the Prussians reach a place called Valmy, which is in the
sentences.zh: 到了9月的第三周，普鲁士人到达了一个叫做瓦尔米的地方，位于

sentences.en: Argonne ForeSt.
sentences.zh: 阿尔贡森林。

sentences.en: It's about 120 miles from Paris.
sentences.zh: 距离巴黎大约120英里。

sentences.en: And rain is falling.
sentences.zh: 雨在下着。

sentences.en: The skies are overcaSt.
sentences.zh: 天色阴沉。

sentences.en: And it's against this very kind of turbulent backdrop that the Duke of Brunswick and the
sentences.zh: 正是在这种动荡的背景下，不伦瑞克公爵和

sentences.en: Prussians turn to finish off the French and to clear the battlefield for their final assault on the capital.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士人转身去消灭法国人，为他们对首都的最后进攻清理战场。

sentences.en: And Tom, what happens next will change the course of European history.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，接下来发生的事情将改变欧洲历史的进程。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太精彩了。

sentences.en: What a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 真是个悬念。

sentences.en: So much more to come.
sentences.zh: 还有更多内容。

sentences.en: Lots more drama.
sentences.zh: 还有很多戏剧性的情节。

sentences.en: And of course, if you are a member of the Rest is History Club, you can listen to the next three episodes of this epic journey to the climax of the French Revolution right now.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果您是“历史的休憩”俱乐部的会员，您可以立即收听这段通往法国大革命高潮史诗旅程接下来的三集。

sentences.en: We will be discussing in our next episode, Olymp de Gouges, the first feminist, the author of The Rights of Woman.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下一期节目中讨论奥兰普·德古热，第一位女权主义者，《妇女权利宣言》的作者。

sentences.en: We will be discussing the fall of the French monarchy.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论法国君主制的倒台。

sentences.en: And the climax will be the guillotining of Louis XVI.
sentences.zh: 而高潮将是送路易十六上断头台。

sentences.en: So it's one of the great stories, not just of French history, but of history, full stop.
sentences.zh: 所以这是最伟大的故事之一，不仅是法国历史上的，而且是整个人类历史上的。

sentences.en: And if you're not a member of the Rest is History Club, then you can listen to the next episode on Olymp de Gouges this coming Thursday.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是“历史的休憩”俱乐部的会员，那么您可以在本周四收听关于奥兰普·德古热的下一集。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for listening.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 拜拜。
